walkthroughs.body_html:
The Black Death was a deadly disease, almost certainly the bubonic plague.

It was caused by tiny bacteria that lived in black rats and the fleas on them. When fleas bit people, they passed it on.

Victims got fever, vomiting and painful black swellings called buboes in their armpits, neck and groin. Most died within a week. 💀

The plague is thought to have started in Asia in the 1330s.

It spread along trade routes — by camel, cart and ship — across Asia and into Europe by 1347.

It arrived in England in June 1348, probably on a ship at Melcombe Regis in Dorset. From there it spread along roads and rivers. 🚢

There were really two main forms:

  • Bubonic plague — spread by flea bites; victims got buboes; about 70% died.
  • Pneumonic plague — attacked the lungs; spread by coughing; almost everyone died.

In the dirty, crowded medieval towns the plague spread very quickly. Doctors had no idea what was really causing it.

mcqs.q: Why was the founding of the NHS controversial in 1948?
options: The British Medical Association opposed nationalisation of doctors; Bevan made concessions allowing private practice; Conservatives feared cost and central control.
The NHS was supported by all parties and all doctors from the start.
The NHS was originally only for soldiers returning from WWII.
Versailles caused WWII because it required Germany to invade Poland.

mcqs.q: Why did the Treaty of Versailles cause resentment in Germany?
options: The NHS was originally only for soldiers returning from WWII.
Because Germany lost more soldiers than any other country in the war.
Because Germany was not invited to sign it.
It assigned sole war guilt to Germany (Article 231) and imposed harsh reparations, territorial losses and military restrictions.

mcqs.q: Did the Treaty of Versailles directly cause WWII?
options: Versailles caused WWII because it required Germany to invade Poland.
The NHS was originally only for soldiers returning from WWII.
Versailles caused WWII directly because it was so harsh on Germany.
It contributed via German resentment and economic strain, but the 1930s Depression, Hitler's choices, and Allied appeasement were equally necessary — Versailles alone is not sufficient.
